candidate: restored-halftime-policy-v1; prior graded costs/thresholds unchanged; no selection from single-slider or package winners
scope: Four synthetic templates, matched and +/-0.35 opponent rating gaps, neutral/maximal tactical roots, 16 fresh seeds per profile with balanced focal orientation. First halves play naturally. Other modifiers disabled for isolation.
primary: Focal-only policy minus neither adapting, focal pre-match win probability. One primary comparison. Conservative 95% difference interval from Bonferroni-combined exact Clopper-Pearson bounds for the two discordance probabilities.
secondary: Both adapting, opponent-only, interactions, score margins, adoption by halftime score/deficit/quality/root/orientation and selected recipes are descriptive. Do not interpret all-Hold cases as a policy effect or evidence of optimal Hold.
mechanicalAcceptance: Identical first-half event histories across paired arms
Native scoring, clocks, energy, eligibility and statistics audit every outcome
Two independent observation-based decisions after native halftime/personnel review
At most two sliders changed, total root distance <=2, values in 1..5
No hidden opponent ratings/fatigue or future results in observations
Exact replay of first two trials per profile/arm (192 outcomes)
No automatic retry, sample expansion, seed replacement, outcome-based threshold tuning or official writes
interpretation: This validates functional behavior and estimates isolated effects on these fixed synthetic profiles; release still requires broader/persistent-fatigue scenarios and holistic v2 testing. Lack of directional statistical evidence does not authorize changing thresholds.
preflight: Separate two side-balanced cases / eight outcomes and exact replays, excluded from scientific sample.
